title: Symmetric difference with a singleton is an involution
statement: Fix $n \in \bbn$ and an index $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$. The map on subsets of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that sends each set $S$ to its symmetric difference $S \triangle \{i\}$ with the singleton $\{i\}$ is an involution: applying it twice returns every set to itself, so $\bigl(S \triangle \{i\}\bigr) \triangle \{i\} = S$ for all $S$.
hypotheses_covered: fixed index $i$ among the $n$ possible indices
replaced:
For a fixed $i$, the map $S \mapsto S \triangle \{i\}$ on subsets of
$\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ is involutive.
